summary: The paper extends the Markov-ICL analysis framework (Edelman et al., 2024) from transformers to Mamba/Mamba-2, showing empirically and via constructive proof that a single-layer Mamba can implement the Bayes/minimax-optimal Laplacian (add-β) estimator on random Markov chains, and identifies the convolution as the key architectural component. A complementary lower bound argues that any finite-precision recurrent model needs hidden dimension·precision ≥ Ω(2^k) to represent the k-th order Laplacian estimator, and language-modeling experiments provide modest external validation of convolution's role. The contribution is solid and reasonably clean but incremental in framework, with theory that is essentially first-order and language experiments that are limited in scope.
strengths: A clean, non-trivial constructive proof (Theorem 1) that MambaZero exactly represents Laplacian smoothing for first-order chains, with the construction empirically grounded in what the trained model actually learns (a_t ≈ 1, b(ij)^T c(t) ≈ 0 when i ≠ x_t), which is a strong theory–practice bridge.

A matching representational lower bound (Theorem 2) that d·p ≥ Ω(2^k(1-3ε)log(1/ε)) for any recurrent model of any depth, which yields a genuine architectural insight (Mamba scales exponentially in Markov order while transformers scale linearly).
A well-designed ablation isolating the role of convolution, including a minimal 'MambaZero' baseline that matches full Mamba, and a clean prediction (w ≥ k+1) that is empirically verified in Fig. 3b.

The switching-Markov experiment gives a persuasive demonstration that the selectivity gate a_t serves the exact function the theory predicts (it goes to 0 at the switch token), extending the story beyond stationary Markov data.
Empirical study is well-controlled: fixed test sequences, direct L1/KL comparison to the optimal Bayes predictor, error bars over 5 seeds on the main figure.

key_concerns.issue: The main theoretical result (Theorem 1) covers only first-order Markov chains, but the paper repeatedly implies a general story for higher orders. Higher-order behavior is asserted from Fig. 1b and 3b alone, and the construction in Sec. 4.2.1 explicitly notes that all key structural facts 'hold for any k ≥ 1' without proving it. The gap between the first-order theorem and the k-order claims is larger than the exposition suggests.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either extend the constructive proof to general k (even sketched, with explicit dimension/parameter counts consistent with the 2^k lower bound), or restate the abstract/intro to make clear that the exact representational theorem is first-order and higher-order results are empirical.

key_concerns.issue: The 'convolution is the key' claim generalizes broadly (Sec. 5.2, abstract), but the supporting language experiment is a single dataset (WikiText-103) at a single small scale (~14M params), with a modest 11% relative perplexity change that further shrinks with depth (Table 5, appendix). This is thinner evidence than the framing suggests, especially since the appendix notes deeper Mamba blocks can approximate convolution.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report at least one additional dataset/scale, hold parameter count constant more tightly across ablated variants, and reframe the language-modeling section as 'suggestive evidence' rather than a generalization of the Markov finding.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is uneven: 5 seeds and std shading are shown for Fig. 1, but tables (e.g., Table 1) report point estimates only, and per-metric variability in the closeness-to-L_β ablations (Fig. 3) is not clearly quantified. Given the modest absolute differences on WikiText-103, no significance claim can be assessed.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report seeds, standard deviations, and paired significance tests for all headline numeric comparisons, including Tables 1, 4, 5.

key_concerns.issue: The transformer 'baseline' is under-specified. It is compared as 1-layer vs 2-layer softmax attention (plus a linear-attention note), but critical settings — head count, width matching, whether the same convolutional preprocessing is added, positional encoding choice — are not visible in the main text. Since one of the paper's more provocative claims is that 1-layer Mamba tracks the optimum more sharply than a transformer, this comparison needs to be watertight.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Detail the transformer configurations in the main text (matched parameter count, matched training budget, matched tokenization), and include a matched 1-layer conv+attention control to test whether convolution — not attention vs. SSM — is the operative variable.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty is real but incremental. The Markov-ICL framework, the Laplacian/add-β target, and the 'induction-head from counting' narrative are all directly imported from the Edelman/Nichani/Rajaraman line for transformers; the paper's genuinely new content is the Mamba construction and the 2^k lower bound. The intro slightly over-sells the framework contribution.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Sharpen Sec. 1 and Related Work to clearly demarcate imported machinery vs. new theoretical results, and foreground Theorem 2's architectural implication as the strongest novel piece.

key_concerns.issue: MambaZero's Prediction layer uses L1 normalization instead of softmax (adopted to ease proof), and the paper does not verify quantitatively that trained full Mamba with softmax behaves identically to the L1-normalized construction on the same sequences. The theorem-to-experiment identification therefore relies on visual matching in Fig. 1a plus qualitative structure matching in Figs. 4–5.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a numeric probe (e.g., KL divergence to Laplacian and to the theoretical MambaZero construction) for the trained full Mamba across many test sequences and seeds, not only a single fixed test sequence.

questions_for_authors: Can Theorem 1 be extended to general k? What is the minimal (d, N, w) as a function of k and S, and does it match the 2^k lower bound of Theorem 2 tightly, or is there still a gap?
In Fig. 3a, is the 'Mamba without convolution' variant matched in parameter count to full Mamba/MambaZero, and are all three trained for the same steps with the same optimizer schedule and seeds?

For the transformer baselines in Fig. 1 and the language experiments, are widths/heads/params matched to Mamba, and did you consider a 1-layer attention + convolution control to disentangle convolution from the SSM/attention axis?

Do the empirical facts you use in the construction (a_t ≈ 1 everywhere, b(ij)^T c(t) ≈ 0 for i ≠ x_t) hold across seeds and hyperparameters, and how sensitive are they to over-parameterization, weight decay, or Dirichlet parameter β?

In the switching-Markov experiment, does a_t actually go to zero *at* the switch token or also at neighbors due to convolution smoothing, and does this affect the counts stored in H_t across a switch?

For the lower bound (Theorem 2), what is the constant hidden in the Ω, and does the argument require the pointwise ℓ∞ guarantee, or does it extend to expected-KL guarantees which would match the training loss more closely?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly appropriately scoped — the paper explicitly notes that learning dynamics are out of scope and that higher-order results are empirical — but the abstract and Sec. 5 'convolution is fundamental on language too' framing outruns the WikiText-103 evidence and should be tempered.

significance.justification: A useful, well-executed extension of Markov-ICL analysis to Mamba, with an architectural-scaling implication (2^k vs linear-in-k) that the community will find interesting, though the practical downstream impact is modest.

novelty.justification: First application of the Markov-ICL framework to Mamba/SSMs and the first exact construction of an add-β estimator in a selective SSM, but the framework, target predictor, and narrative style are directly inherited from prior transformer-ICL work.

rigor.justification: The constructive proof is careful and empirically anchored to the model's learned structure, and the lower bound argument is clean; the main soundness gap is that Theorem 1 is first-order while higher-order claims are only empirical.

statistical_soundness.justification: Main figure reports std across 5 seeds, but seeds/variance are inconsistently reported for the language-modeling tables and the appendix ablations where the numeric margins are small.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations (representation-only, no dynamics; first-order theorem; not a full architectural comparison) are stated, though the 'convolution is fundamental' framing over-generalizes from a single language-modeling dataset.

clarity.justification: The problem, the estimator, and the construction are explained clearly and the proof sketch in Sec. 4.2.1 is easy to follow; notation for the Mamba recurrence is dense and the OCR-rendered extraction has some layout artifacts, but the underlying prose is readable.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure (Intro, Related Work, Setup, Theory, Beyond Markov, Conclusion) with appropriate length and clear delineation of theory vs. experiments.

reproducibility.justification: Data generation, loss, optimizer, architecture equations, and construction parameters (N=S, d=2S, e=1, w=2) are specified; several important knobs (transformer baseline width/heads, exact Mamba hyperparameters, WikiText-103 training budget) are deferred to appendices summarized only briefly here.

related_work.justification: Positioning against transformer-ICL Markov work and prior Mamba-ICL empirical studies is clear, but the comparison to Rajaraman et al. and Sanford et al. is asserted rather than analyzed, and the absence of a reference list (expected under anonymization) makes it hard to judge coverage.

figure_quality.justification: From the captions, figures are purposeful and evidentiary: Fig. 1 compares to the Bayes-optimal predictor, Fig. 3 isolates convolution, Fig. 3b maps window size to Markov order, and Fig. 13 visualizes the switching gate; they support claims rather than decorate.

breadth_generality.justification: Theory is first-order only, higher-order support is empirical, and the beyond-Markov section rests on one synthetic switching task plus one small-scale language dataset — insufficient to underwrite the general 'convolution is fundamental' framing.

overall_recommendation.justification: A solid, borderline-accept contribution: novel-for-Mamba analysis, a clean construction that matches learned structure, a genuine lower bound, but incremental relative to the transformer-Markov line and thin on higher-order theory and language-scale evidence.
